headline: From the Kid Who Didn't Know What LinkedIn Was
deck: SkillBridge is run by two high schoolers who figured out the professional world from the inside. This is how we got here, and why we're handing the map to the teens right behind us.
pullQuote: We're a few steps ahead of you, not above you. Close enough to remember exactly what it felt like to be behind.

sections.heading: It started with not knowing
paragraphs: A couple of years ago Skyler didn't know what LinkedIn was. No clue how a resume was supposed to look, or how anyone his age was supposed to talk to an adult who ran a company.
School never taught that part. So we started figuring it out the slow way, one awkward step at a time.

sections.heading: Then we built Padre Professionals
paragraphs: That figuring-out turned into a club. Padre Professionals grew into the largest club on our campus, 160+ members strong.
Running it changed us. We learned how to talk to adults, invite guest speakers, and walk into a room without feeling like we didn't belong. The confidence was the real thing we built.

sections.heading: The confidence led to real rooms
paragraphs: That confidence turned into internships and real conversations with people we used to be too nervous to email. Recruiters, CEOs, people who work at LinkedIn.
Everything we teach comes from that network. It's not theory pulled off a blog. It's what actual professionals told us works.

sections.heading: So we built SkillBridge
paragraphs: SkillBridge is the public version of all of it. Skyler and David teaching other teens the things school skips — LinkedIn, resumes, interviewing, networking, college prep.
We also run a Discord. It's a separate, smaller community, around 35 teens right now and still growing, where people trade what's working and ask the questions nobody answers in class.
No paywalls. No gatekeeping. Just the moves nobody bothered to show us, handed over plainly.

sections.heading: Why we keep doing it
paragraphs: High school can feel confusing. The aimlessness, the college anxiety, the quiet sense that everyone else got a manual you missed. We felt all of it.
Our mission is to turn that into direction. One teen learning this stuff opens a door for the next one, and the network keeps growing.

closingLine: Gen Z teaching Gen Z. We lived the gap, and now we're closing it for the people right behind us.
